leaders.priorTitle: Vice Provost for Academic Initiatives and External Affairs
leaders.notes: Fourth chancellor of UM-Dearborn (Jan 1993-1999); left to become president of North Carolina A&T State University (1999-2006). Died in 2019 at age 72; the campus University Center was renamed in his honor.

leaders.priorTitle: Professor Emeritus of Political Science and Public Administration
leaders.notes: Served as interim chancellor (July 1999-June 2000) between Renick's departure and Daniel Little's arrival.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Professor (returned to faculty, Ford School of Public Policy)
leaders.notes: Fifth chancellor (2000-2018), a philosopher of social science; his 18-year tenure was the longest in campus history and he remained on the faculty afterward.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Chief Academic Officer
leaders.notes: Sixth chancellor (August 2018-May 2025), an environmental engineer; departed on May 8, 2025 to become interim president of the University of Michigan (Ann Arbor).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Became interim chancellor May 8, 2025 after Grasso's departure, then was named permanent (seventh) chancellor in May 2026 following a national search, with a five-year appointment effective May 22, 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Longtime UMSL administrator who rose from associate dean of faculties to chancellor; named interim chancellor in 1990 and chancellor in April 1991, retiring December 2002. The Blanche M. Touhill Performing Arts Center is named for her.

leaders.priorTitle: Deputy to the Chancellor
leaders.notes: Served as interim chancellor between Touhill's December 2002 retirement and Thomas George's September 2003 arrival; a longtime UMSL business administrator.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.nextRole: Chancellor Emeritus / Professor of Chemistry and Physics
leaders.notes: UMSL's longest-serving chancellor (September 2003-2019); a chemist who had been chancellor at UW-Stevens Point for seven years. Remained at UMSL as chancellor emeritus.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs (later Executive Vice Chancellor)
leaders.notes: Joined UMSL as provost in 2017; became interim chancellor in 2019 and the eighth chancellor in April 2020. An anthropologist, she previously was a dean at Wright State University. Stepped down effective July 1, 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Research and Economic and Community Development; Professor of Chemistry
leaders.notes: Named interim chancellor effective July 1, 2026 after Sobolik's departure; a UMSL chemist with more than 35 years at the university. The UM System is conducting a national search for a permanent chancellor.

leaders.priorTitle: Professor and Dean of Education
leaders.notes: Chancellor 1977-1997; guided UNO's transformation into a metropolitan university. Chancellor emeritus; died in 2019 at age 86.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.notes: First woman to serve as UNO chancellor (1997-2006); came from Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, where she had been its first woman president/chancellor.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Academic and Student Affairs
leaders.notes: First UNO alumnus to serve as chancellor; interim chancellor from Sept 12, 2006, appointed chancellor May 2007, served through 2017. Died May 2025 at age 76.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor, University of Nebraska Medical Center (held concurrently with UNO)
leaders.nextRole: President (2024); continued as UNMC Chancellor after leaving UNO
leaders.notes: Served as UNO chancellor 2017-2021 (interim from May 2017) while simultaneously chancellor of the University of Nebraska Medical Center; became the ninth University of Nebraska system president in 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Business
leaders.notes: 16th chancellor, since July 2021; first woman of color to lead UNO and first Asian American in a University of Nebraska system executive leadership role. In 2023 became the system's first endowed chancellor (Barbara and Wally Weitz Endowed Chair in Higher Education).

system: University of Louisiana System (rejoined the LSU System as 'LSU New Orleans' effective July 1, 2026)

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Chancellor 1987-2003 under the LSU System (title was 'Chancellor' throughout his tenure); earlier provost at University of South Florida and at University of Michigan-Flint.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Business Administration (Hibernia Professor of Economics)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to UNO faculty (professor of economics)
leaders.notes: Chancellor 2003-2010, an economist who had been UNO's business dean. Removed as chancellor by the LSU System in 2010 amid post-Katrina enrollment and budget struggles.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Acting/interim chancellor from September 2010; led UNO through its 2011 transfer from the LSU System to the University of Louisiana System. Died in 2020.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: First UNO leader to hold the title 'President' (sixth chief executive), 2012-2016, after the university joined the University of Louisiana System. Retired in 2016.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: President 2016-2023; joined UNO as provost in 2015 (previously provost and vice chancellor at Southern Illinois University Carbondale). Left to become president of Florida Tech.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Interim president July 1-November 1, 2023, bridging Nicklow's departure and Kathy Johnson's arrival.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice Chancellor and Chief Academic Officer
leaders.notes: Eighth president and first woman to lead UNO (Nov 1, 2023). Steered the university through a financial crisis and its transition back to the LSU System, then stepped down June 30, 2026 to become EVP and provost at Saint Louis University (effective July 13, 2026).

leaders.priorTitle: Interim Chief Administrative Officer
leaders.notes: Named interim chancellor and chief administrative officer effective July 1, 2026, as the university rejoined the LSU System and rebranded as 'LSU New Orleans'; the head-of-campus title reverted from 'President' to 'Chancellor.' A national search for a permanent chancellor is underway.

university: University of North Carolina at Greensboro

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
leaders.notes: Ninth chancellor and first woman to lead UNCG (January 1, 1995-2008). Died in 2009 at age 69.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President and Provost
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
leaders.notes: Tenth chancellor (2008-2015), a political scientist who was previously provost at the University of Oregon and dean at NC State; earlier led Georgia Tech's Sam Nunn School of International Affairs. Retired July 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
leaders.nextRole: Returned to Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
leaders.notes: Acting chancellor from March 2015 until Gilliam's September 2015 arrival; had joined UNCG as provost in 2014 (previously provost at University of Texas at Arlington).

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Luskin School of Public Affairs
leaders.notes: Eleventh chancellor, since September 8, 2015; a political scientist who previously spent seven years as dean of UCLA's Luskin School of Public Affairs. No successor search announced as of mid-2026.
